edition.locus: Gebhardt XII.V (frankincense and a shoot; Tartarus answered)

source_text: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ τύραννος· Εἰ ἔγνως τὸν Χριστόν, γνῶθί τε καὶ τοὺς ἡμετέρους θεούς. Ἐμοὶ πείσθητι καί, μὰ τοὺς θεοὺς ἅπαντας, τιμὴν οὐ τὴν τυχοῦσαν περιποιήσεις σεαυτῷ, ἀλλὰ καὶ εὐγενῆ πίστιν καὶ δόξαν ἐν γενεᾷ. Οὐ λέγω σοι θῦσον, ἀλλ᾽ οὐδέ τι τῶν τοιούτων ποίησον. Μόνον δὲ λάβε λίβανον βραχὺν καὶ οἶνον καὶ θαλλὸν καὶ εἰπέ· Ὕψιστε, σῶσε τὸ πλῆθος τοῦτο. Τοῦτο εἰπέ, καὶ ἕτερον οὐδέν σε ἐπάγω. Ἐμοῦ ἄκουσον παρακαλοῦντός σε καὶ φύγε τὴν ἀσεμνοτάτην θρησκείαν. Τί πλανᾶσθε, ἄνθρωπον θεὸν λέγοντες, καὶ τοῦτον βιοθανῆ; Ὡς ἔμαθον παρὰ Ἰουδαίων ἀκριβῶς, καὶ τί τὸ γένος αὐτοῦ καὶ ὅσα ἐνεδείξατο τῷ ἔθνει αὐτῶν καὶ πῶς ἀπέθανεν σταυρωθείς. Προκομίσαντες γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὰ ὑπομνήματα ἐπανέγνωσάν μοι. Παῦσαι οὖν τῆς τοιαύτης μωρίας καὶ ἔσο μεθ᾽ ἡμῶν εὐφραινόμενος. Ὁ δὲ μακάριος μάρτυς στενάξας καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, πρὸς τὸν τῶν ὅλων θεὸν προσευξάμενος, τῷ τυράννῳ ἔφη· Ἀσεβέστατε πάντων ἀνθρώπων, εἴθε τοιαύτης μωρίας καὶ σὺ ἧς μετέχων καὶ μὴ ἀπώλλεις ψυχάς, ἃς οὐκ ἔδει ἀπολέσθαι, προσέχων λίθοις ἀψύχοις καὶ ἔργοις χειρῶν ἀνθρώπων, τοῖς μὴ βλέπουσιν μήτε ἀκούουσιν. Πῶς δὲ ἐτόλμησας τὸν ἐπὶ πάντων θεὸν οὕτω βλασφημῆσαι, οὗ ἐν χερσίν ἐστιν ἡ πνοή σου; Ἐμοὶ δὲ γένοιτο καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐπικαλουμένοις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἀνεξαρνήτως ἀεὶ ὑμνεῖν καὶ δοξάζειν αὐτὸν τὸν τῶν ὅλων σωτῆρα καὶ θεόν. Καὶ ὁ ἀσεβὴς τύραννος μεμηνὼς ἐπὶ τοῖς λεχθεῖσιν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου μάρτυρος λέγει πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐμοὶ οὐ πείθῃ, αἱ βάσανοί σε πτοῆσαι πείσουσιν· εἰ δὲ καὶ τῶν βασάνων καταφρονεῖς, λέοντί σε πικροτάτῳ παραβαλὼν οὕτως σε ἀναλώσω, ἢ βορὰν τοῖς ἐκ βυθοῦ θηρίοις παραδώσω σε, ἢ ἐπὶ σταυροῦ κρεμάσας ἀποκτανθῆναί σε ποιήσω, ἢ λαβροτάτῳ πυρὶ ἐν λέβητι ὑποκαιομένῳ βαλῶ σε καὶ ἐκτήξω τὰς σάρκας σου, ἐὰν μὴ θύσῃς τοῖς ἀηττήτοις καὶ αἰωνίοις θεοῖς. Καὶ ὁ μακάριος μάρτυς λέγει πρὸς τὸν ἀσεβῆ τύραννον· Ἀσχημονεῖς, ἡγεμών· λόγοις ἐπαγγελλόμενος μόνον, ἐκφοβεῖν με οἰόμενος, νομίζεις πεῖσαί με; Οὐ πείσεις με, μὴ γένοιτο. Βλέπε δὲ μή σε ὁ κριτὴς ταρτάρῳ παραδώσῃ ἀνυπερθέτῳ, ἢ πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ εἰς αἰῶνας, ὅπου ὁ σκώληξ οὐ τελευτᾷ καὶ τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται. Αἱ γὰρ σαὶ βάσανοι, ἃς ἐπαγγέλλῃ μοι, οὐ δύνανταί με ἀδικῆσαι· θεὸν γὰρ ἔχω τὸν ἐνδυναμοῦντά με. Ὁ δὲ τύραννος εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Εἰ καὶ αἱ βάσανοι οὐδὲν ἰσχύσουσιν κατὰ σοῦ, ἔτι πικροτέρας βασάνους ἐπινοήσομεν κατὰ σοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: The tyrant spoke to him: if you knew Christ, know also our gods; obey me and, by all the gods, you will gain for yourself no chance honor but noble standing and glory in your generation; I do not say sacrifice nor do any such thing; only take a little incense and wine and a sprig and say, Highest, save this crowd; say this and I put nothing else upon you; listen to me entreating you and escape the most disgraceful cult; why are you deceived, saying a man is God, and he one who died an untimely violent death; as I learned exactly from Jews both his descent and what he showed to their people and how he died being crucified, for bringing his records they read them to me; stop then such folly and be rejoicing with us; and the blessed martyr groaned and looked to heaven and prayed to the God of all and said to the tyrant: most impious of all men, would that you shared such folly and did not ruin souls which ought not perish by giving heed to lifeless stones and works of human hands which neither see nor hear; how dared you thus blaspheme the God over all in whose hands is your breath; but to me and to all invoking his name may it be given to sing and glorify always without denial him the Savior and God of all; and the impious tyrant maddened by the holy martyr's words said to him: if you are not persuaded by me, tortures persuading you to fear will persuade; and if you scorn even tortures, throwing you to a most savage lion I will so consume you, or give you as prey to beasts from the deep, or hang you on a cross and cause you to be killed, or throw you into fiercest fire kindled under a cauldron and melt your flesh, unless you sacrifice to the unconquered eternal gods; and the blessed martyr said to the impious tyrant: you behave indecently, governor; only making promises with words and supposing to terrify me, do you think to persuade me; you will not persuade me, may it not happen; see lest the judge deliver you to Tartarus without postponement, or to unquenchable fire unto ages, where the worm does not end and the fire is not quenched; for your tortures which you promise me cannot injure me, for I have God who empowers me; and the tyrant said to him: even if tortures avail nothing against you, we shall contrive still more bitter tortures against you.
pass_b_english: The tyrant said to him: If you have come to know Christ, know our gods also. Be persuaded by me and, by all the gods, you will procure for yourself no ordinary honor, but noble credit and glory among your generation. I do not tell you to sacrifice, nor to do any such thing. Only take a little frankincense and wine and a branch and say: Most High, save this multitude. Say this, and I lay nothing else upon you. Hear me as I urge you and flee this most shameful religion. Why do you go astray, calling a man God, and him one who died a violent death? As I learned accurately from the Jews, both what his lineage was and what he displayed to their nation and how he died after being crucified. For they brought forward his records and read them aloud to me. Cease therefore from such folly and be rejoicing with us. But the blessed martyr groaned and looked up to heaven and prayed to the God of all, then said to the tyrant: Most impious of all men, would that you too shared in such folly and did not destroy souls that ought not to perish by attending to lifeless stones and works of men's hands that neither see nor hear (Psalms 115:4-6). How did you dare so to blaspheme the God over all, in whose hands is your breath (Daniel 5:23)? But may it be granted to me and to all who call upon his name to hymn and glorify him without denial forever, the Savior and God of all.

And the impious tyrant, enraged at what was said by the holy martyr, says to him: If you are not persuaded by me, the tortures will persuade you into terror. But if you even scorn the tortures, by exposing you to a most savage lion I will thus consume you, or I will hand you over as prey to the beasts from the deep, or after hanging you upon a cross I will have you put to death, or I will cast you into fiercest fire kindled under a cauldron and melt your flesh, unless you sacrifice to the unconquered and eternal gods. And the blessed martyr says to the impious tyrant: You act shamefully, governor. By merely promising with words and supposing to frighten me, do you think you will persuade me? You will not persuade me, God forbid. See lest the Judge hand you over to Tartarus without postponement, or to unquenchable fire forever, where the worm does not end and the fire is not quenched (Mark 9:48). For your tortures, which you promise me, cannot harm me, for I have God who strengthens me (Philippians 4:13). And the tyrant said to him: Even if the tortures will have no power against you, we shall devise still more bitter tortures against you.

choices.english: one who died a violent death
choices.why: adjective marks an untimely or violent death, fitting the tyrant's contempt for a crucified man, not neutral mortality
vocative address plus imperative with demonstrative multitude preserves the imposed token acclamation without making it Christian prayer
dative adjective modifies Tartarus as immediate irrevocable delivery, answering the tyrant's repeated threats of devised tortures
